name: Forensic Disk Imaging
description: Ability to create forensically sound images of storage media including HDDs, SSDs, NVMe drives, USB devices, and RAID arrays. Covers write-blocking, imaging formats (E01, AFF4, dd), integrity verification, and dealing with damaged or encrypted media. Foundational to all disk-based forensic work.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to forensic disk imaging

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands why forensic imaging differs from standard copying and the importance of write-blocking
evidence: Can explain the difference between a forensic image and a file copy
Understands the role of write blockers in preserving evidence integrity
Can describe common forensic image formats (E01, dd, AFF4)

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Creates forensic images of standard media under supervision using established procedures
evidence: Successfully imaged HDDs and USB devices using FTK Imager or dc3dd under guidance
Correctly connected and verified hardware write blockers before imaging
Computed and recorded SHA-256 hashes at acquisition time
Documented imaging process in case notes reviewed by authorized personnel

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently images a range of storage media with full procedural compliance and chain of custody documentation
evidence: Independently imaged 10+ evidence items across HDD, SSD, NVMe, and USB media
Imaging logs and hash verification records pass QA audit without findings
Handles both hardware and software write-blocking appropriately per media type
Produces acquisition reports that meet lab and legal standards

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Images complex and damaged media; handles encryption, RAID, and degraded drives; mentors junior examiners
evidence: Successfully imaged degraded drives using ddrescue or similar recovery tools
Handled RAID reconstruction and imaging of multi-disk arrays
Imaged encrypted media (BitLocker, FileVault, LUKS) with appropriate key management
Reviews imaging procedures and acquisition logs of junior staff
Contributed to lab imaging SOP updates

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines lab imaging methodology; handles novel storage technologies; supports legal challenges to evidence admissibility
evidence: Authored or maintains the lab's forensic imaging methodology
Validated imaging procedures for new storage technologies (e.g., UFS 4.0, CXL memory)
Provided expert testimony or declarations on imaging integrity and methodology
Trains teams on forensic imaging procedures and troubleshooting

assessment_methods.description: Image a provided drive using a write blocker, verify hashes, and produce an acquisition report within lab SOP requirements
Audit acquisition reports and hash verification logs from recent casework
